content.text: One of the first computers in Austria made available for academic research is set up in the newly constructed Neues Institutsgebäude (NIG) at the Department of Statistics.
The NIG building itself is a separate date:

.

For size, I found only directory figures, and they describe different things. One directory gives the building, not the data centre:

citations.cited_text: The building Vienna University Computer Center (Wien) sits in has a footprint of 42,001 sq ft, which is about 3,902 square meters.
citations.title: Vienna University Computer Center (Wien) Data Center in Vienna

content.text: the building the facility sits in has a footprint of 42,001 sq ft, which is about 3,902 square meters.
The NIG houses many institutes, so this is probably the whole building rather than the server space. Another directory describes the data centre itself:

content.text: it offers over 900 square meters of space and is equipped with 2MVA of power.

I used the building figure because the building type takes priority, but the 900 m² figure may better reflect the facility. Neither figure comes from the operator, so treat the size as low confidence.

The ZID's own pages confirm the location:

citations.cited_text: Der ZID betreibt mehrere zentrale Serverräume an der Universität Wien – 2 davon befinden sich im Kellergeschoß des Neuen Institutsgebäudes (NIG).
citations.title: IT-Infrastrukturprojekte des ZID (in German) - Universität Wien

content.text: the ZID operates several central server rooms at the University of Vienna, 2 of which are in the basement of the Neues Institutsgebäude (NIG).
